remediation.title: What Do Animals and Plants Need to Live?

sections.title: Stage 1 foundations
sections.description: First ideas about living things, growing plants, our senses, materials, forces and sound from Stage 1.

questions.question: What do all plants need to grow well?
questions.options: sweets, toys and books | sand, glass and glue | wool, paper and paint | light, water and air
questions.explanation: Plants are living things. They need light, water and air to make their food and grow well.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What Do Animals and Plants Need to Live?

questions.question: A frog lives by a pond, where it finds food, water and shelter. What do we call the place where an animal lives and finds what it needs?
questions.options: a holiday | a habitat | a market | a machine
questions.explanation: A habitat is the home of an animal or plant — the place where it finds the food, water and shelter it needs.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What Do Animals and Plants Need to Live?

questions.question: Sara wants to find out if a plant needs light. She puts one plant in the sun and one in a dark cupboard. What should she keep the same for both plants?
questions.options: the names she gives the plants | the number of leaves they lose | the amount of water they get | the amount of light they get
questions.correctAnswer: the amount of water they get
questions.explanation: To make the test fair, only the light should be different. Everything else, like the water, must stay the same for both plants.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What Do Animals and Plants Need to Live?

questions.question: Which of these is a natural rock you could find outside?
questions.options: plastic | paper | granite | glass
questions.explanation: Granite is a rock made by nature. Glass, plastic and paper are materials that people make.

questions.question: Why do builders often use rock to make walls?
questions.options: Rock melts in the rain | Rock is soft and bendy | Rock is hard and strong | Rock floats away in the wind
questions.explanation: Rock is a hard, strong material, so walls made of rock stand up well and last a long time.

questions.question: Amina scratches two rocks with a coin. One rock gets a scratch mark and the other does not. Which rock is harder?
questions.options: the rock with a scratch | the prettier rock | the rock with no scratch | the smaller rock
questions.explanation: A harder rock is more difficult to scratch. The rock the coin could not mark is the harder one.

questions.question: A bar of chocolate is left in the warm sun. What happens to it?
questions.options: It turns into water | It grows bigger | It freezes and becomes hard | It melts and becomes soft
questions.explanation: Warming chocolate makes it melt — it changes from solid to soft and runny. Cooling it makes it hard again.

questions.question: Water is put in a freezer and left overnight. What does it change into?
questions.options: milk | ice | sand | steam
questions.explanation: When water gets very cold it freezes and turns into solid ice.

questions.question: Which of these changes can be undone (reversed)?
questions.options: burning paper | frying an egg | baking a cake | freezing water into ice
questions.explanation: Ice can melt back into water, so freezing can be undone. A baked cake, burnt paper and a fried egg cannot change back.

questions.question: Which of these is a source of light?
questions.options: a mirror | a book | a spoon | the Sun
questions.explanation: The Sun makes its own light, so it is a light source. A mirror only bounces light that comes from somewhere else.

questions.question: What is a shadow?
questions.options: a dark shape made when something blocks light | a picture drawn with a pencil | a reflection in the water | a bright light behind an object
questions.correctAnswer: a dark shape made when something blocks light
questions.explanation: When an object blocks light, the light cannot pass through, and a dark shape — a shadow — appears behind it.

questions.question: You are in a room that is completely dark, with no light at all. What can you see?
questions.options: everything clearly | only bright colours | nothing | only big things
questions.explanation: We can only see when light enters our eyes. With no light at all, we can see nothing.

questions.question: Which of these needs electricity to work?
questions.options: a torch | a paper book | a wooden spoon | a woolly hat
questions.explanation: A torch uses electricity from its batteries to make light. The spoon, book and hat work without any electricity.

questions.question: A circuit has a battery, wires and a bulb, but the bulb does not light because there is a gap in the circuit. What should you do?
questions.options: take the battery out | join the wires to close the gap | shake the bulb hard | add another gap
questions.correctAnswer: join the wires to close the gap
questions.explanation: Electricity can only flow around a complete circuit. Closing the gap lets the electricity flow, so the bulb lights up.

questions.question: Which of these is a SAFE thing to do with electricity?
questions.options: poke a socket with a metal fork | ask a grown-up before using a plug socket | pull a plug out by tugging its wire | use a hairdryer close to bath water
questions.correctAnswer: ask a grown-up before using a plug socket
questions.explanation: Mains electricity is powerful, so always ask a grown-up first. Metal and water must never go near sockets.

questions.question: Why is it daytime on our side of the Earth?
questions.options: The clouds are making the light | The Sun has switched off | The Moon is covering the Sun | Our side of the Earth is facing the Sun
questions.correctAnswer: Our side of the Earth is facing the Sun
questions.explanation: It is daytime when our side of the Earth faces the Sun. When our side turns away from the Sun, it becomes night.

questions.question: The Sun seems to move across the sky during the day. What is really moving?
questions.options: the clouds, which push the Sun along | the Sun, which circles the Earth each day | the Moon, which pulls the Sun | the Earth, which is spinning
questions.explanation: The Earth spins round once each day. That spin makes the Sun seem to travel across the sky, even though the Sun stays put.

questions.question: Which of these is a living thing?
questions.options: a stone | a goat | a chair | a cup
questions.explanation: A goat moves, eats, grows and breathes, so it is alive. Stones, chairs and cups are not living.

questions.question: Which of these can ALL living things do?
questions.options: drive cars | sing songs | grow | read books
questions.explanation: Every living thing grows — plants, animals and people. Reading, driving and singing are only things some people do.

questions.question: What does a seed need so it can start to grow?
questions.options: music | paint | sweets | water
questions.explanation: A seed needs water to wake up and start growing into a little plant.

questions.question: Which part of a plant grows down into the soil?
questions.options: the leaves | the flower | the fruit | the roots
questions.explanation: The roots grow down into the soil. They hold the plant steady and drink up water for it.

questions.question: Which body part do you use to see?
questions.options: your nose | your feet | your ears | your eyes
questions.explanation: You see with your eyes. Your ears hear, your nose smells and your feet help you walk.

questions.question: You listen to a bird singing in a tree. Which sense are you using?
questions.options: hearing | tasting | smelling | touching
questions.explanation: Listening uses your sense of hearing. Your ears catch the sounds the bird makes.

questions.question: Which material is a window usually made from?
questions.options: mud | wool | glass | paper
questions.explanation: Windows are made from glass because glass is see-through and lets the light in.

questions.question: Which material would be best for making a warm jumper?
questions.options: metal | wool | stone | glass
questions.explanation: Wool is soft and keeps warmth in, so it is perfect for a jumper. Glass, metal and stone are hard and cold.

questions.question: You kick a football and it rolls away. What kind of force did you use?
questions.options: a pull | a push | a sound | a smell
questions.explanation: Kicking the ball pushes it away from you. A push moves things away; a pull brings things closer.

questions.question: You open a drawer by moving it towards you. What kind of force is that?
questions.options: a pull | a bounce | a drop | a push
questions.explanation: Moving something towards you is a pull. Pushing the drawer shut would be a push.

questions.question: How can you make a drum sound louder?
questions.options: hit it harder | move it far away | cover it with a blanket | hit it more softly
questions.explanation: Hitting the drum harder makes bigger vibrations, and bigger vibrations make a louder sound.
